scope: Theorem 7.1 (Hidden propagation) of the manuscript “Cutoff throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase” (preprints/Cutoff-throughout-the-high-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-phase-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d99d391c8c3ed79f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 67. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let λsp be the spin spectral edge in Theorem 6.7. For every z < λsp there is a finite constant Cz with the following property. Fix t ≥ 1, and let u = u(X0) and p = p(Xt) be polynomially bounded endpoint vectors with bounded second moments. Suppose that u is hidden, p = df is an exact gradient, and E ∑︂ j wj(Xt) ∥djp(Xt)∥2 ≤ Ct < ∞ (7.1) uniformly along the dimension sequence. Then lim sup n→∞ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓Eut Ktp ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ≤ Cze−zt lim sup n→∞ (︁ ∥u∥2 ∥p∥2 )︁ . (7.2) The constant does not depend on the bound in Equation (7.1); that bound is allowed to depend on the fixed time t. Equivalently, the rate on the right is exp[−(λsp − o(1))t], with the dimension limit taken first. The assertion also holds in the integrated deterministic-time and mask comparisons of Theorems 5.1 and 6.1.
